title: Air India Takes Delivery of Fourth Custom-Built Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner
excerpt: The aircraft, registered VT-AWD, completes Air India's initial batch of bespoke Dreamliners as the airline prepares 156 weekly widebody departures for the Northern Winter season.
body:
• VT-AWD, Air India's fourth line-fit Boeing 787-9, landed in India this week, completing the airline's initial batch of custom-built Dreamliners
  • The four new-build aircraft will operate Delhi-Toronto, Mumbai-Dubai and Mumbai-London Heathrow routes this Northern Winter season
  • Air India plans 156 weekly widebody departures across nine sectors, with 26 legacy 787-8s undergoing retrofits through mid-2027
  • Each line-fit 787-9 carries 296 seats across Business, Premium Economy and Economy with Recaro seating

Air India has taken delivery of its fourth factory-configured Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, registered VT-AWD, which landed in India earlier this week. The aircraft completes the airline's initial batch of custom-built widebody jets, joining VT-AWA, VT-AWB and VT-AWC in what has become the centrepiece of the Tata-owned carrier's fleet transformation.

A Fleet Built From Scratch

The line-fit 787-9 programme represents Air India's first bespoke widebody order since privatisation. Unlike the six 787-9s inherited through the Vistara merger in November 2024, these aircraft were designed to Air India's specifications, with cabin interiors installed directly on Boeing's production line in Everett, Washington.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=b_L1u77BwLw

The first of the four, VT-AWA, arrived in Delhi on January 12, 2026, after a nonstop ferry flight of 16 hours and 58 minutes from Boeing's Everett factory. It entered commercial service on the Mumbai-Frankfurt route from February 1, though its early months were complicated by a seat-certification delay that blocked 18 economy seats from sale.

Winter Deployment: Three Sub-Fleets, Three Missions

With VT-AWD's arrival, Air India will operate its Boeing 787 fleet as four distinct sub-fleets this Northern Winter, which takes effect October 25. According to data from aviation analytics firm Cirium, shared exclusively with Network Thoughts, the four line-fit 787-9s will anchor three key routes: Delhi-Toronto at seven times weekly, Mumbai-Dubai at nine times weekly, and Mumbai-London Heathrow at seven times weekly.

The six ex-Vistara 787-9s, carrying 299 seats each, are concentrated on the two busiest European corridors — Delhi-Frankfurt at 13 times weekly and Delhi-London Heathrow at 17 times weekly. Meanwhile, refurbished 787-8s handle a mix of Delhi-Bengaluru, Mumbai-Frankfurt, Mumbai-London Heathrow and Delhi-Tokyo Haneda services.

Between them, the airline will run 156 weekly widebody departures across nine sectors — with no two sub-fleets sharing an identical mission profile.

"2026 will see a total of six widebody aircraft deliveries, including Airbus A350-1000 and Boeing 787-9. The new cabins will become the new benchmark across our Boeing 787 fleet."

— Air India

Inside the New Cabin

Each line-fit 787-9 is configured with 296 seats across three classes: 30 in Business, 28 in Premium Economy and 238 in Economy. The aircraft features Recaro seating throughout Premium Economy and Economy cabins — a noticeable upgrade from the older fleet. The configuration differs from the ex-Vistara 787-9s, which carry 299 seats with a smaller 21-seat Premium Economy cabin.

The Bigger Picture

The new-build deliveries sit within a broader fleet overhaul. Air India is simultaneously retrofitting 26 legacy Boeing 787-8 aircraft, converting them from dual-class to three-class configurations with modernised interiors and the airline's updated livery. The retrofit programme is expected to be completed by mid-2027. Once finished, nearly 60 percent of Air India's widebody fleet will feature modern interiors.

Air India had planned six total widebody deliveries in 2026, spanning both Airbus A350-1000 and Boeing 787-9 aircraft. With VT-AWD now delivered, the airline has completed its line-fit 787-9 intake and can turn its attention to integrating the remaining widebody arrivals.

What It Means for Diaspora Travellers

For passengers on the Delhi-Toronto route — one of the most-travelled corridors for the Indian diaspora in North America — the line-fit 787-9 represents Air India's best available product. The seven-times-weekly frequency signals the airline's commitment to the ultra-long-haul Canada market, where it competes directly with Air Canada. The Mumbai-London deployment adds another layer of premium product on a route already served by ex-Vistara jets from Delhi, giving Heathrow-bound travellers from both major Indian metros access to Air India's newest cabins.
